title: Server-side request forgery
brief: 16:50. A new feature shows a preview card for any link a customer pastes. The server fetches the page to build it. It runs inside Veltrix's cloud.
role: Platform engineer, reviewing a change on the Veltrix engineering team
insight: The server will fetch whatever it is told to, from inside the network, with the network's trust.
teaches: A server that fetches user supplied URLs can be pointed at things only it can reach
Allowlist what may be fetched, and block internal and link-local addresses after resolving the name
A string blocklist for “localhost” loses to decimal, hex and DNS tricks

value.title: Link preview service

lines: const page = await fetch(target);              // follows redirects
The portal runs on a cloud VM with an instance role.
The metadata service at 169.254.169.254 hands out the role credentials.
The admin console listens on localhost:9000 on the same machine.

fix.prompt: Pick every change that limits what the server can be made to fetch, and any that limits what a stolen credential could do.

options.label: Only fetch http and https URLs to an allowlist of hosts we choose
options.why: Deciding what may be fetched, rather than what may not, is what works.

options.label: Resolve the host first and refuse private, loopback and link-local addresses
code: + // then connect to that same ip: no second lookup
options.why: This catches the internal targets however they are spelled, including names that resolve inside.

options.label: Require a session token for the metadata service and cut the role down to what the portal needs
code: + role portal-role: allow only storage:read on veltrix-portal-assets
options.why: If a request still reaches the metadata service, a plain fetch gets nothing, and what it could reach is small.

options.label: Reject URLs containing "localhost" or "169.254"
options.why: Attackers write the address as 2852039166, 0xA9FEA9FE, or point a DNS name at it. String blocklists lose.

options.label: Add a two second timeout to the fetch
options.why: Good hygiene, but it does not change where the request can go.

outcome.label: Read the vulnerable code first
outcome.what: Reading the code before attacking it tells you where to look, and why it fails.
outcome.ideal: reads the code under review before trying to break it.

outcome.label: Tried normal use first
outcome.what: Knowing what a good request looks like is how you spot a bad one.
outcome.ideal: establishes normal behaviour before testing the abnormal.

outcome.label: Checked normal use still works
outcome.what: A fix that breaks real users gets reverted, and the bug comes back.
outcome.ideal: tests that the fix did not break normal use.

outcome.label: Reproduced the bug
outcome.what: The preview feature fetched the metadata address from inside the cloud and returned the response: the server's temporary credentials. With those, an attacker acts as the portal against the cloud account.
outcome.ideal: proves a bug is real before fixing it.

card.title: The server gave away its own keys
body: The preview feature fetched the metadata address from inside the cloud and returned the response: the server's temporary credentials. With those, an attacker acts as the portal against the cloud account.
The request came from a customer. The server made it, from a place customers cannot reach.
card.ideal: reproduces a bug first, so the fix can be proved to work.

fix.objective: Fix it: pick the changes on the Fix tab that close the hole for good, then apply the patch.

label: Picked everything that fixes it? Apply the patch
Pick every change that fixes the cause
Open the Fix tab

hint.text: Pick every change that removes the cause. Avoid changes an attacker can walk around, and ones that do not touch the problem. Then Apply the patch.

outcome.label: Applied a real fix
outcome.what: An allowlist means the server cannot be steered to an internal address at all. Resolving the name and refusing private and link-local ranges catches the tricks, and the metadata service now needs a token and a much smaller role.
outcome.ideal: fixes the cause, not the symptom.

card.title: The server fetches only what we chose
body: An allowlist means the server cannot be steered to an internal address at all. Resolving the name and refusing private and link-local ranges catches the tricks, and the metadata service now needs a token and a much smaller role.
Three layers, each one enough to stop the demo.
card.ideal: fixes the cause with the standard control, and adds defence in depth.

outcome.label: Applied a fix that can be bypassed
outcome.what: Blocking the words localhost and 169.254 stops the obvious spelling. The same address can be written as a single decimal number, in hex, or as a name that resolves there, and a redirect can bounce through.
outcome.ideal: fixes the cause instead of blocking one payload or hiding the symptom.

card.title: The blocklist is a puzzle, not a wall
body: Blocking the words localhost and 169.254 stops the obvious spelling. The same address can be written as a single decimal number, in hex, or as a name that resolves there, and a redirect can bounce through.
Decide what is allowed, rather than what is not.
card.ideal: fixes the cause, and knows why a blocklist or a hidden field is not a fix.

outcome.label: Applied a patch that was not enough
outcome.what: The patch missed part of the fix, or added a change that does not address the problem.

card.title: Not enough
body: The patch missed something that has to change, or included a change that does nothing for this bug. Open the Fix tab to see which options were right, missed, or wrong, and why.
A partial fix is the most dangerous kind: everyone assumes it is closed.

verify.objective: Prove it: re-run the exploit on the Exploit tab, then check normal use still works.

label: Send the exploit again: it should be blocked
Open the Exploit tab

hint.text: On the Exploit tab, send the exploit again. It should be blocked. Then send the normal request to check nothing broke.

outcome.label: Proved the exploit is blocked
outcome.what: The same request that worked before now fails, and normal use still works.
outcome.ideal: verifies a fix by re-running the exploit.

card.title: Fixed, and proved
body: You re-ran the exact request that broke it, and it is blocked. A fix you have not tested against the exploit is a hope, not a fix.
Add the exploit as an automated test so nobody can quietly bring the bug back.
card.ideal: turns the exploit into a regression test.

outcome.label: The exploit still works
outcome.what: The patch did not close the hole. The same kind of request still gets through.
outcome.ideal: never ships a fix without re-running the exploit.

card.title: Still open
body: The exploit still works after your patch. This is what happens when a fix blocks one payload, or hides a symptom, instead of removing the cause.
Go back over the Fix tab: it shows which options were right, and why the others fail.
card.ideal: verifies with the exploit before calling it fixed.
